angles.title: Who to email
angles.why: Most of your 50 emails went to the wrong people; a tight list fixes reply rate before you touch copy.

angles.title: Pick one narrow segment first
angles.why: A 60-person startup and a 450-person company have different sales leaders; pick one and write for them only.

angles.title: Hiring and change signals
angles.why: A VP who posted 5 SDR jobs this month is 10x more likely to book than one picked at random.

angles.title: Build and verify the list
angles.why: You need 300 to 500 verified contacts a month, and over 3% bounces gets your domain flagged.

angles.title: The offer and positioning
angles.why: A vague product pitch to a sales leader gets deleted; a specific outcome for their team gets a reply.

angles.title: Find the pain in their words
angles.why: Talk to 5 sales leaders before writing; their exact phrases become your first line and your promise.

angles.title: One specific promise, not features
angles.why: Sales leaders reply to a number they miss, not to a feature list.

angles.title: The ask: 15 minutes or teardown
angles.why: A 15-minute look or a free teardown of their outbound gets 3x the yes of asking for a demo.

angles.title: Use the founder angle
angles.why: I built this and want your take gets replies a sales rep never will; use it while you still can.

angles.title: Writing the email
angles.why: Your one reply in 50 came from the words; better words at the same volume gets you 5 to 10.

angles.title: Subject line and first line
angles.why: A short plain subject plus a first line about them is what shows in the preview and decides the open.

angles.title: Under 80 words, one ask
angles.why: Busy leaders read on a phone; one observation, one promise, one question, nothing else.

angles.title: Personalization without hours
angles.why: You cannot hand-write 400 emails a month, so learn which one line to personalize.

angles.title: Landing in the inbox
angles.why: At volume, half your emails can silently go to spam, and you would never know.

angles.title: Secondary domains, inboxes, warmup
angles.why: Two lookalike domains, 2 inboxes each, 20 to 30 sends a day per inbox, warmed for 2 weeks before you send.

angles.title: SPF, DKIM, DMARC
angles.why: Missing records is the top reason cold email gets filtered before opening.

angles.title: Plain text, no links, no tracking
angles.why: Open-tracking pixels, links, and images in a first email cut inbox placement; send it like a person would.

angles.title: Test inbox placement before sending
angles.why: Send each new template to your own Gmail and Outlook seeds first; spam there means spam everywhere.

angles.title: Opt-out line and the law
angles.why: One opt-out line, a real address, and honoring every no keeps your domain and company out of trouble.

angles.title: Follow-up sequences
angles.why: Most replies come on email 2 to 4, and one-and-done is why 50 emails got 1 reply.

angles.title: Cadence: 3 to 5 steps
angles.why: 3 to 5 touches over 2 weeks roughly doubles replies versus a single email.

angles.title: Follow-ups and the breakup
angles.why: Just checking in gets ignored; each step needs a new reason, and the last one asks if you should close the file.

angles.title: Add a LinkedIn touch
angles.why: A profile view or connect the day before email 1 lifts replies, and it costs nothing.

angles.title: Turning replies into meetings
angles.why: A reply is not a meeting; the handoff is where beginners lose half of them.

angles.title: Reply within the hour, book now
angles.why: Interest fades in hours; answer fast and offer two times or a link in the first reply.

angles.title: Handling not now and send info
angles.why: Half of replies are soft nos, and a good response turns some into meetings.

angles.title: Qualify, confirm, cut no-shows
angles.why: Ask team size before booking, then send a reminder the morning of; that saves 1 in 4 meetings.

angles.title: Running it week to week
angles.why: 5 meetings a month comes from sending every day and knowing which stage is leaking.

angles.title: The funnel math to 5 meetings
angles.why: At 5% replies and 25% of replies booking, 5 meetings needs about 400 sends; know your numbers.

angles.title: The daily sending routine
angles.why: 20 to 25 new contacts a day, every workday, beats a 200-email burst once a month.

angles.title: Find which stage is broken
angles.why: Under 1% replies is deliverability or list, 1 to 3% is copy; at your volume change one thing per 200 sends, not A/B tests.

angles.title: Pick one sending tool
angles.why: One tool that runs sequences and rotates inboxes frees your time for copy, not spreadsheets.

angles.title: Scaling past 5 meetings
angles.why: Going from 5 to 15 meetings means more domains and inboxes, not longer emails.
